judged.root_cause_verdict:
Confirmed. The framework has a direction-convention error; the model did not cause it. LIBERO writes left/right/front/behind from the external agentview camera's point of view. In all 6 problem classes that camera sits at +x, y=0, looking toward -x, so image-right is world +y. Every directional BDDL region and direction word fits right=+y, left=-y, front=+x (toward the camera), behind=-x, with 0 counterexamples (41/41 decidable checks, 31 anchored side regions).

uc7 hard-codes right_of=+x, left_of=-x, behind=+y, front_of=-y. That is LIBERO's frame rotated -90 deg, so all four words are wrong in LIBERO, not only right_of. The constant is written in three places:
- the planner prompt, /workspace/gpt_field/src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check_spatial.py:59-60
- the region resolver, same file :211-214
- the review UI, /workspace/gpt_field/src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check.html:104-105 and :244

On top of that, METRIC_INSTRUCTIONS ("State the frame ... do not assume image left/right is world -x/+x", /workspace/gpt_field/src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check_client.py:133-135) pushes the planner to write world axes. The executive gets no definition at all.

The planner's own pointing was on the correct side: cell 55 ray-casts to about (0.11, 0.18), which is +y. It still wrote right_of with the part text "table: surface to the plate's world +x side". The executive followed that text and released the pudding at (0.29, -0.02).

Swapping the constant would not fix it. RoboCasa's world axes rotate with the layout (robot yaw = fixture.rot + pi/2), and the current table fits RoboCasa layout 0 only by coincidence. The general fix is one direction definition based on the external camera, computed from calibration by code and used by the planner text, the executive data, the resolver and the UI.

Two related gaps:
- The plan-time wrist image is not rotated (k=0), although the prompt says it matches image 1. In LIBERO it is 180 deg off.
- A region with null bounds means the whole far half-plane, not LIBERO's adjacent 10x10 cm box (this is the D9 decision).

The same constant also drove the v3 LIBERO-goal g5 plans (front_of the stove).

designGeneral.design_name: External-view reference frame for spatial relations: the code converts the words using camera calibration, and the model does no frame conversion
designGeneral.summary:
ROOT CAUSE
- The wrong meaning of the direction words is hard-coded in three places:
  - the planner prompt, spatial.py:59-60 (right_of=+x, behind=+y);
  - the resolver, spatial.py:211-214;
  - the review UI, agent_speedup_v2_user_check.html:104-105 and :244 ('Right of anchor (world +x)').
- The plan request carries no calibration: its fields are request/task/holding/images/status in review/requests/000001. The planner can only obey the rule.
- The planner copied the rule into its part text: 'table: surface to the plate's world +x side'.
- The executive receives that plan verbatim as the reviewed goal (agent_client.py:477-480; region frame 'world'). It released the pudding at (0.29,-0.02).
- Why the rule is wrong for LIBERO:
  - The external camera sits at +x and faces the robot (libero_living_room_tabletop_manipulation.py:188-191). The robot base is at x=-0.51 (on_the_ground_panda.py:47-50).
  - Image-right is world +y: calibration R[:,0]=(0,1,0) in the t4, t5 and t6 requests.
  - Every LIBERO directional task definition follows that camera, with 0 counterexamples:
    - right=+y in 23 region instances, left=-y in 5, front=+x in 3;
    - every left/right/front/back object adjective;
    - the libero_goal 'front of the stove' region.
- Why it is wrong for RoboCasa: the robot's yaw is fixture.rot+pi/2 (kitchen.py:680). So no fixed world-axis table can be right there.

DESIGN
- Every directional relation carries an explicit reference frame, frame='external_view'. It means 'as seen in the external camera image':
  - right_of / left_of: toward image-right / image-left of that camera;
  - behind / front_of: farther from / nearer to that camera, along the support surface.
- The planner only copies the words from the task sentence. It does no conversion and writes no world axes or coordinates.
- Code builds the frame from the external calibration:
  - right_xy = unit(horizontal part of R[:,0]);
  - away_xy = up x right = (-r_y, r_x);
  - for LIBERO this gives (0,1) and (-1,0).
- The frame is frozen at the reviewed reset and used in three places:
  1. The resolver. The half-plane test (p-o).d > max over the anchor of (v-o).d replaces the axis tests; it is identical to them when d is a world axis. Bounds are given in view axes.
  2. The executive. The first request gains view_frame and region_frames, which carry world unit vectors. The executive never converts words itself and never reads task directions from the wrist image.
  3. Plan-time wrist turning. prepare_review passes external=None, so every review checked used k=0. That contradicts the prompt's 'turned so that its left and right match'. The exact calibration gives k=2.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED
- Swap the axis table to right=+y: correct for LIBERO only.
- Give the planner calibration and ask for world-direction text (the prior S4(a) proposal): keeps a model-side conversion and a second, prose contract. That prose channel is exactly what failed here.
- Let the model write direction vectors: same problems.
- Ground regions from the model's pointing:
  - too coarse: cell 55 ray-casts to y=0.181, beyond the y<=0.15 limit;
  - often missing: E has x=0 in t6_009 and t6_011;
  - sometimes arbitrary: t6_006 pointed at bare table on the -y side;
  - it cannot re-ground when the anchor moves.
- Screen-space regions: distorted by perspective and cannot express metric adjacency.
- Pointing is kept only as advisory evidence.

NOTICING A FRAME MISMATCH WITHOUT VETOES
- (a) Pointing evidence. Take the image-1 displacement from the anchor's cell to the region's cell and map it onto the support plane through the camera's horizontal axes. Project it on the relation direction and classify at grid resolution: agrees / disagrees / indeterminate / unpointed. Under the old rule this run would have shown 'disagrees' (score -33.8). Under the new rule it shows 'agrees' (+128).
- (b) The review UI prints the code-computed world direction next to each relation.
- (c) A convention test over each benchmark's task definitions, run when a suite is onboarded.
- (d) An executive guideline: after a finish request that does not end the episode, re-check what each spatial goal means.
- None of these re-asks the model or blocks anything.

OPTIONAL D9 (adjacency; your decision)
- Rule: a side relation with no bounds means 'beside the anchor'. The region is limited to a lateral band equal to the anchor's measured extent, and the aim is the nearest fitting free cell next to the anchor's edge. No new constants.
- Evidence it recurs beyond one run:
  - 8 LIBERO goal regions are 0.1 m squares centred on the anchor;
  - t6_007 first released at y=0.198 and t6_009 ended at y=0.170, both past the y<=0.15 limit;
  - in the official layout the pudding starts at (-0.040,0.117). That is already inside the plain half-plane, but LIBERO does not count it as right of the plate.

Rule 1 (one frozen build):
- One frozen code version and one global convention for every task.
- The frame is a deterministic function of the external-camera calibration, an allowed input.
- No task key, simulator object or goal region reaches the agent. region_frames is derived only from calibration plus the model's own plan.

Rule 2 (general capability, no breakage):
- This is a general capability: relations tagged with their reference frame. It is justified by every LIBERO direction task (0 counterexamples across all BDDL files) and by RoboCasa's layout-dependent yaw, not by t6 alone.
- Recorded successes are not touched structurally: t4_001, t5_001, t5_002 and the relayout t7 have regions [], so the resolver change does not apply to them.

Rule 3 (fix the gap, not the task): the failure is treated as a framework gap with a general fix. The gap is a hard-coded convention, no frame representation, and an uncalibrated wrist turn.

Rule 4 (remove vetoes, avoid thresholds):
- Removes a hard-coded axis table and the world-axis prose channel.
- Adds no veto: pointing evidence is advisory and never an issue or re-ask.
- Adds no tuned threshold: D9 uses the anchor's measured extent and the existing M16 floor; pointing evidence is classified at the pointing grid's own resolution.
- The only validation change replaces the frame enum value and the absolute-bounds reading.

designMinimal.design_name: Viewer words from external-camera calibration (smallest uc7 fix: one definition and one helper, shared by prompt, executive, resolver and UI)
designMinimal.summary:
ROOT CAUSE. Three places use one hard-coded world-axis constant (right_of=+x, left_of=-x, behind=+y, front_of=-y): the planner prompt (spatial.py:59-60), the review UI labels and note (html:104-105, 244) and the region resolver (spatial.py:210-214). The executive gets no definition of these words. It copies the planner's "world +x" text (direction_semantics_audit.json, accepted_decisions ordinals 1, 8, 11, 12 and 14).

The constant is wrong for LIBERO wherever it was used:
- Relayout t6 released the pudding at (0.29, -0.02).
- In t6_006, the native resolver itself placed region E at (0.234, -0.009), on the +x side (user_check_framework.json /state/entities/E/region_evidence).
- t6_009 wrote "world +x side" and released at (0.30, 0.02).
- LIBERO-goal g5 ("push the plate to the front of the stove", v3 g5_001/002) used front_of, which the constant maps to -y. The BDDL stove_front_region is +x of the stove: (-0.05, 0.21) against the stove region at (-0.41, 0.21).

LIBERO's own convention:
- Every problem class puts agentview at +x, y=0, looking toward -x. So image-right is +y and "toward the camera" is +x.
- My offline scan found 31 anchored left/right/front/back regions in 26 BDDL files (libero_10 and libero_90). All of them, plus g5, follow this: right = +y, left = -y, front = +x. There are 0 exceptions.
- The caddy's back compartment is at world -x (local +x, caddy yaw pi).

The planner's own pointing already follows the viewer reading. Of the 5 recorded regions whose pointing can be judged, 4 agree with the viewer reading and none with the constant (pointing_agreement.py).

DEFINITION GIVEN TO THE MODEL. left_of, right_of, front_of and behind are viewer words, as the task sentence uses them, and are judged in image 1 (the external camera):
- right_of / left_of: next to the anchor, toward image 1's right or left edge.
- front_of / behind: next to the anchor, nearer to or farther from that camera, along the support surface.

Why this definition:
- It is the convention the task sentences are written in.
- It is what the model already sees.
- It can be computed from the camera calibration the rules already allow.
- A robot-centric definition would be mirrored in LIBERO, because the robot faces +x and its right is -y.
- The old constant matches RoboCasa layout 0 only by coincidence (within 12 degrees).

MECHANISM. Add one pure helper, viewer_axes(geometry):
- right = normalize(R_ext[:2, 0]), the image-right column of rotation_world_from_camera projected onto the floor plane.
- front = (right_y, -right_x) = right x up, which points toward the camera.
- LIBERO gives (0, 1) and (1, 0). RoboCasa agentview_left gives (0.979, -0.202) and (-0.202, -0.979).

Both the resolver and the executive context use this helper. The prompt, the executive instructions and the UI labels state the same rule. The plan request gets no new input and the schema does not change. There are no extra model calls and no new thresholds or vetoes.

HOW A FUTURE MISMATCH WOULD SHOW, WITHOUT GATES:
- Offline tests pin the convention to the LIBERO BDDL files and to saved calibrations.
- The region evidence records direction_world_xy and the viewer axes.
- The executive's first request carries the computed direction.
- Optionally, a sign-only pointing cue (region cell vs. anchor cell) is stored in the review record and shown in the UI.
- An offline post-run audit can compare the final pose with the direction.
- None of these block a run or trigger a re-ask.

Effort: about 1.5-2 h including offline tests.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT:
- An adjacency or extent default for regions with null bounds (decision D9). The half-plane stays, so a native place_on to E could still land beyond LIBERO's 10 cm box.
- Bounds in viewer axes. Bounds stay world metres, and the prompt asks for null bounds with the four direction words.
- Calibration in the plan request, and any conversion of words to axes by the planner.
- Schema or enum changes ("frame" stays "world"; no new words such as beside or between).
- The wrist-turn defect. At plan time the wrist image is shown with k=0, which in LIBERO is turned 180 degrees from the external view, while the base prompt says it is turned to match. Making k come from calibration would change every LIBERO plan image, so it is deferred.
- Freezing the axes at plan time. Both adapters have a static external camera.
- The repair and review prompts of the older ReviewedV2Policy, and the frozen v3 executive.
- Any runtime check, re-ask or automatic correction.

designMinimal.rule_compliance: R1: One build and one definition, computed only from the external-camera calibration that is already supplied. There is no task key and no benchmark constant, and the threshold table is unchanged; the helper's only numeric guard is that image-right has a horizontal component. R2: This is a general relation-semantics capability, not a t6 patch. The mechanism recurs on 2 tasks in 2 suites: LIBERO-10 t6 (prompt in t6_009/011/relayout, native resolver in t6_006) and LIBERO-goal g5 (front_of). RoboCasa adds a structural reason, since its world axes vary by layout. The recorded successes t4_001, t5_001/002, relayout t7 and RoboCasa coffee all have regions=[], so only their prompt text changes. t6_007 succeeded because the executive read the task the viewer way, which the fix makes explicit. For LIBERO the resolver change is a relabelling of its four existing tests. R3: It fixes the class: prompt, executive, resolver and UI share one helper and one wording; no t6 coordinates are involved. R4: It removes a wrong constant and adds no veto, re-ask or threshold. The pointing cue and audits are passive evidence only. R5: It is organised by mechanism (direction semantics end to end) and accepted by the all-task sweep on one frozen build. Old approvals are invalidated automatically, because claim compares runtime hashes (agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:396-397).

A native place_on to E aims near the half-plane centre and can overshoot y_max = 0.15, because D9 (adjacency default) is excluded.

Prompt changes affect every task. SPATIAL_INSTRUCTIONS is appended to every plan and replan (client.py:374-379), and AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS goes into every executive call. So t4, t5, t7 and RoboCasa plans could change for unrelated reasons; only the sweep can show there is no regression.

The planner may still write a world-axis phrase, since METRIC_INSTRUCTIONS asks it to 'State the frame'. The explicit ban and the authority of region_directions mitigate this, but a gap remains if the executive trusts the text over the field.

The design assumes task language is written from the external camera's viewpoint. This holds for all 31 anchored LIBERO direction regions and g5, and RoboCasa's camera looks along the robot's heading. A future benchmark with robot-centric wording and a camera facing the robot would invert left and right.

Axes are read from the current observation. That is only correct while the external camera is static (LIBERO's fixed agentview; RoboCasa with the base held). A moving camera would rotate the region's meaning during an episode.

The wrist 'turned to match' claim stays false in LIBERO at plan time (k=0). Region wrist cells may be pointed wrongly, as in the relayout (w=29). That is harmless for grounding and the executive today, but misleading for any future user of those cells.

items.item: P0.1 Calibration-derived support-plane vectors (right = normalize(R[:2,0]), away = normalize(-R[:2,2])) as the single source of truth
items.reason: Using the external camera is correct. LIBERO language follows the external viewer, and the viewer faces the robot, so viewer-right is the robot's left. A robot-base frame would also be wrong. Three parts of the formula and its use need changing. (1) away = -R[:2,2] becomes ill-conditioned as the camera approaches top-down; image-up projected (R[:2,1]) or the support-plane Jacobian at the anchor pixel is equal when roll is 0 and stays well-conditioned. (2) The vector must be frozen at plan approval. RoboCasa's external camera is robot-mounted, and a replan must keep reviewed regions verbatim. (3) It must be code-owned data shown everywhere, never model-written prose.

items.item: P0.2 Planning prompt: viewer-frame definition plus per-scene numeric mapping, with region text stating both
items.reason: This is the change that fixes the observed failure. Part text is what carries the semantics to the executive. Two runs had part text naming world +x (relayout, t6_009), and both made the first pudding release on +x. t6_011's text was 'world right of striped plate' and it never moved the pudding. t6_007's axis-free text ('table: bare top surface') went to +y and succeeded. Six problems remain. (a) The planner has no calibration today: the review initial_observation.json holds only images, state and prompt, so plumbing is needed. (b) The numbers belong in request fields, not in static instructions, which are built once in __init__. (c) Asking the model to write world axes makes the executive depend on model frame arithmetic, the same channel that failed. Have code render the axis. (d) Vertical words and object-intrinsic part words must be exempted. (e) The same prompt falsely says the wrist image is turned to match the external image. (f) A 'frame':'world' value next to a viewer relation invites a 'world right = +x' reading.

items.item: P0.5 Zero-call ray-cast sign test of the region part's pointed cell against the anchor
items.reason: Unsound as a gate; acceptable only as a diagnostic. (1) The prompt defines x as 'the part's cell'. For a generic 'table: bare top surface' any table cell qualifies: t6_006 pointed at cell 43 → (-0.013,-0.125), which fails a +y test even though right_of is correct under P0. (2) x=0 in 2 of 5 recorded region plans (t6_009, t6_011), so the check cannot run. That 0 was honest: under the old rule the +x side was outside the external view. (3) At plan time the anchor reference is its own coarse cell. C61's centre is 4.7 cm from the true plate centre and C53's is 5.9 cm, against a plate radius of 6.9 cm. A cell covers about 8×7 cm of table in the bottom row and 17×12 cm in row 5. Shared rows or columns give exact ties: t6_007 under the old rule had (E-C).x = 0.000. (4) Plane-height error does not matter between two pointed cells, because positions on any horizontal plane scale about the camera nadir. It matters only against measured geometry. (5) Under viewer semantics the test reduces to image-space ordering of two cells the model picked from the same image, so it is mostly tautological. (6) With PLAN_REASKS=1, a false positive raised as a plan issue can end in invalid_plan, which makes it a veto.

items.reason: The evidence is wider than one task but mixed. Across the 5 anchor-relative LIBERO goal boxes, all suites: lateral alignment with the anchor centre holds 5/5. Placing the centre of mass just past the anchor edge lands inside 4/5 (t6 plate-right, K7 bowl-right, K6 mug-front, STUDY1 caddy-right). It fails for the libero_goal stove-front box, x∈[-0.09,-0.01], about 0.2 m past a stove at x=-0.41 with half-size ≈0.095. The executive's natural placement overshot twice (t6_007 first target y=0.20; t6_009 final 0.170). As written, P0.6 sits in the dormant resolver and has zero effect on uc7. In the native path it needs the held r_obj, so it belongs in aim_target, not region grounding, and _measure_goal still accepts any half-plane cell. Occupied neighbourhoods or a larger object push the spot outward.

items.item: P0.7 Verification: unit test, BDDL alignment harness, plan-only t4/t5/t6, live t6 then t4/t5
items.reason: The ordering is right, but it misses the review wrist-image turn, the all-task effect of the prompt text (the spatial text is appended to every plan request), legacy 'frame':'world' plans, and freezing. Rule 5 accepts only an all-task sweep on one frozen build, so t4/t5 regression alone is not enough. RoboCasa coffee cannot tell the old and new rules apart: there image-right ≈ +x and away ≈ +y, so they nearly coincide. Part of the offline harness is already done: all 7 agentview definitions give right=(0,1), away=(-1,0), and every directional BDDL region and position word aligns.
items.evidence: libero_cams.py output; bddl_dir_tasks.txt (38 files); 40/40 review requests with quarter_turns 0; RoboCasa coffee geometry; plans_summary.txt (regions occur only in t6 plans).
items.modification: Add: (a) unit tests for P0.1 on the LIBERO definitions and the RoboCasa sample, including a degenerate top-down case. (b) A review-image test: the wrist turn k must make wrist image-right ≈ external image-right (k=2 at the LIBERO start pose). (c) Plan-only runs on all 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, asserting no new regions for t3 'bottom drawer', t5 'back compartment', t4 left/right plates and t9 'behind open door', and that the t6 region resolves to +y. (d) Post-hoc truth: the first pudding release is inside x∈[0.10,0.20], y∈[0.05,0.15]. (e) A full 10-task live sweep on one frozen build, including t6 with both the official layout and the relayout. Use the BDDL harness offline only, never to tune constants.

missing_from_p0: False wrist-image claim at review. The plan prompt says 'The wrist image is turned so that its left and right match the external image' (agent_speedup_v2_client.py:197-201), and the image label says 'turned' (:505). Yet request_meta.quarter_turns=0 in all 40 review plan requests across 39 review dirs, because turns() returns 0 when ctx.cal is None (agent_speedup_v2.py:591-596). At every LIBERO-10 start pose, wrist image-right = world -y and external = +y, so images 3/4 are the external view rotated 180°. Left/right words read from the wrist image come out reversed. Fix it with the same calibration plumbing as P0.2.

Plan-time calibration plumbing: R/initial_observation.json has only observation/image, observation/state, observation/wrist_image and prompt, and the plan request fields carry no geometry. The review needs the sim 'agent_geometry' op, and the result should be frozen into review artifacts for reproducibility.

Freezing and storage: the resolved direction should be stored at approval as code-owned data outside the model-echoed region JSON. framework.py:156-161 requires reviewed regions to be preserved verbatim, and PlanLock hashes the plan semantics. RoboCasa's external camera is robot-mounted, so a per-request recompute would rotate the meaning.

Executive contract: framework.py:110 passes regions raw with 'frame':'world' and no definition. Add the resolved vector and the relation frame there. The 'frame' enum (spatial.py:40, :95) is misleading next to viewer relations. Either rename it, which breaks validation of every recorded region plan, or redefine it as the bounds frame and document that.

Review UI: agent_speedup_v2_user_check.html:104-105 labels relations 'Right of anchor (world +x)', 'Behind anchor (world +y)' and so on, and :244 says the words 'follow world axes, not image directions'. A human reviewer would be told the opposite of P0. The default bounds are at :232. agent_speedup_v3.html:104-105 has the same labels.

Part text is the actual carrier of meaning, so do not rely on model-written world axes. Two runs whose text named +x (relayout, t6_009) made their first release on +x. t6_011 ('world right of striped plate') never moved the pudding. t6_007 ('table: bare top surface') went to +y and succeeded.

Exemptions belong in the prompt: vertical words (t3 'bottom drawer', 'top of the shelf', 'under the cabinet shelf') mean world z; object-intrinsic parts (t5 back compartment, t9 'interior cavity behind open door', caddy compartments) are not regions; t4 'left/right plate' is object selection, not a region.

Observability: under the old rule the destination was outside the external camera's view. On the table the image bottom edge is at x≈0.223 and the plate +x edge at 0.218; the release (0.29,-0.02) projects to v≈577 and the t6_006 region centre to v≈521. The planner honestly set x=0 for E in t6_009 and t6_011. A viewer-defined relation keeps the destination in view, which is a general argument for P0. 'Pointed destination not visible' could also be logged as a diagnostic.
bounds_xy_m stays in world axes, relative to the anchor centroid. It must be explained through view_axes_world and shown in the UI in viewer terms; recorded region plans all used null bounds.

Post-finish behaviour: after finish (relayout request 14, step 1065) the executive took the reviewed +x relation as satisfied and switched to centring the mug. AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS:175-177 says to recheck unfinished spatial relations but not against the task sentence. Same root cause: the reviewed text overrode the sentence.
Egocentric trap: the LIBERO agentview sits at x≈+0.61 looking toward the robot, so viewer-right = robot-left. The P0.2 and P0.4 text must exclude the robot's own left/right.
regression_risks: The planner may over-apply the new region definitions to object-intrinsic or selection words: t5 'back compartment', t3 'bottom drawer', t4 'left/right plate', t9 'behind open door'. Today only t6 plans contain regions (plans_summary.txt). Run plan-only checks on all 10 tasks.

P0.5 promoted to a plan issue would produce false positives: generic region pointing (t6_006 cell 43 fails +y) and exact row/column ties. With PLAN_REASKS=1 that can end in invalid_plan, so no episode runs.

P0.6 changes native targeting for every anchored null-bounds relation. Layouts like the libero_goal stove-front box (≈0.2 m past the anchor) would fail, occupied neighbourhoods push the target outward, and _measure_goal still accepts any half-plane cell.

Renaming the 'frame' enum makes every recorded region plan fail validate_spatial_spec (spatial.py:95): t6_006/007/009/011 and the relayout. That affects replays and loading old plans into the review UI.
Putting per-scene numbers into static instructions would make the instructions differ per scene and break PROMPT_VERSION comparability and caching. Use request fields.
Dropping the negative METRIC sentence without a wrist caveat could lead the model to equate wrist-image axes with world axes: wrist image-right = world -y at start and rotates with hand yaw.

RoboCasa: recomputing the mapping per request from the robot-mounted camera would rotate relation meaning if the base moved. In the recorded coffee layout the old and new rules nearly coincide (right≈+x, away≈+y), so that run cannot detect a regression.

P0.3 without P0.6 or bounds would aim the native resolver at a far +y half-plane centroid (estimate, unverified). No recorded success uses the native region path, so nothing recorded regresses, but this must not be counted as a t6 fix.

Recorded successes look safe. t4_001, t5_001, t5_002, relayout task_7 and uc7 relayout t4/t5 have regions [] and viewer-consistent text ('left/right plate', 'rear middle cavity behind low front compartment', 'tall body in front of the other mugs'). t6_007 succeeded with axis-free text and the natural +y reading. No success depended on the +x rule.
rule_conflicts: Rule 4: P0.5 as a plan issue is a new veto with demonstrated false positives (t6_006) and an inconclusive class (x=0 in 2 of 5 region plans; ties). Keep it diagnostic-only.

Rule 2: within LIBERO-10 only t6 needs P0.6. Cross-suite BDDL supports lateral alignment 5/5 and adjacency 4/5, but setting a gap constant from those boxes would be benchmark tuning. It is acceptable only if expressed through the existing measured-clearance rule (M16: r_obj + max(floor, sigma)) with no new threshold.
Rule 1: the BDDL alignment harness in P0.7 uses evaluator ground truth. That is fine as offline verification, but it must never reach the agent or set constants.

Rules 2 and 3: P0.2's request that the model write world axes in part text puts a measurement-rule result into model prose. The general capability is a code-computed axis from calibration shown to the model and the reviewer.

No conflict for P0.1, P0.2 (definition) and P0.4: they use only camera calibration (an allowed input under rule 1). They are a general mechanism recurring across t4 (left/right plates), t5 (back compartment) and t6 (right of plate), plus libero_90/goal wording, which satisfies rule 5.
